Upper Lower Split Workout

The upper/lower split divides training into upper body sessions (chest, back, shoulders, arms) and lower body sessions (quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves). With 4 sessions per week — two upper and two lower — each muscle group receives the training frequency research suggests is optimal for growth, without requiring the 6-day commitment of PPL.

Beginner 📅 4 days/week ⏱ 55–70 min
📚 Professor Splits' Guide

Upper/lower is forgiving: if you miss a session, shift the week rather than doubling up. Keep the first exercise of each day heavy and progress it steadily, and let the accessories absorb the rest of your effort.

Overview

The upper/lower split is one of the most evidence-based workout structures available. It allows you to train each muscle group twice per week on a manageable 4-day schedule, making it ideal for intermediate trainees who want structured, effective training without the high frequency demands of PPL.

The upper/lower split is excellent for intermediate trainees who can train 4 days per week and want a balance of strength and hypertrophy. It is also a strong option for beginners who have already learned the basic compound movements and want to move beyond full-body training.

✅ Pros
  • Each muscle trained twice per week — solid training frequency for growth.
  • Only 4 days per week — sustainable long-term.
  • Good balance of compound and isolation work.
  • Flexible — can be run Monday/Tuesday/Thursday/Friday or any similar pattern.
  • Works well for both strength and hypertrophy goals.
⚠️ Cons
  • Less total volume per session than bro split — you cover more in less time.
  • Sessions can run long if you try to include too much.
  • Not as specialised — bro split and PPL allow more focus per session.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is upper/lower better than PPL?▾
Neither is universally better — it depends on your schedule. Upper/lower is more efficient on 4 days; PPL allows more volume per session on 6 days. If you can do 4 quality sessions per week, upper/lower is excellent. If you have 6 available days, PPL provides more total volume.
Can I run upper/lower on 3 days?▾
Yes, but it becomes either A/B/A one week and B/A/B the next, or you simply repeat one of the sessions. This is less ideal than 4 days but works if your schedule demands it.
How heavy should I go on upper/lower?▾
The "A" sessions in this template are strength-focused (lower reps, heavier weight). The "B" sessions are hypertrophy-focused (moderate weight, more reps). This variation is intentional and produces good results for both strength and size.
